translationRepairs: Once my underling, he showed the grit of Zhong and Yu and the blunt honor of Shi Yu, tightened my slack rule and steeled my cowardice, and saved me from fault—that merit is mine to repay.

Once my underling, he showed loyal and resolute conduct and personally embodied the integrity of Shi Yu, tightened my slack rule and steeled my cowardice, and saved me from fault—that merit is mine to repay.
Chinese 忠毅之操 is loyal-resolute conduct parallel to 史魚之節, not two men named Zhong and Yu.

Formerly, when he was a menial attendant serving with your servant, he displayed the devotion of Zhong and Yu and personally embodied the integrity of Shi Yu, tightened your servant's slack discipline, and stiffened your servant's timidity, so that your servant escaped blame—truly we rely on his merit.

Formerly, when he was a menial attendant serving with your servant, he displayed loyal and resolute conduct and personally embodied the integrity of Shi Yu, tightened your servant's slack discipline, and stiffened your servant's timidity, so that your servant escaped blame—truly we rely on his merit.
Chinese 忠毅之操 names virtues, not persons Zhong and Yu; only 史魚 is a person.
One dawn at the kitchen a gale struck; she ran to the hall and begged leave to go home to her parents.
One dawn at the kitchen a gale struck; she ran to the hall and begged her mother-in-law for leave to go home and take leave of her two parents.
After 從姑求歸, 辭其二親 means bid farewell to her own parents, not parents-in-law.

One morning when she went to the cook-shed, suddenly a violent wind sprang up; the woman at once went up to the hall and begged her mother-in-law to let her return home, taking leave of both parents-in-law.

One morning when she went to the cook-shed, suddenly a violent wind sprang up; the woman at once went up to the hall and begged her mother-in-law to let her return home, taking leave of her two parents.
辭其二親 refers to her birth parents after asking the mother-in-law for leave to return.
Once ill, he rose from bed to return a maid's courtesy sent by Chen Shi's wife.
Once when he was ill, his wife sent a maid to bow and inquire; he got down from the bed and returned the bow.
Chinese 妻遣婢 is Fan Ying’s own wife sending a maid; the idiomatic English wrongly attributes the wife to Chen Shi.
Sun Ling flattered the palace eunuchs under Emperor Ling and rose to minister of education.
His grandson Ling, in Emperor Ling’s time, by flattering the eunuchs became minister of education.
孫陵 means “grandson Ling,” not a man surnamed Sun; Fan Ying’s grandson is at issue.
Sun Ling, in the time of Emperor Ling, by fawning on the eunuchs became minister of education.
Grandson Ling, in the time of Emperor Ling, by fawning on the eunuchs became minister of education.
Same kinship misread: 孫陵 is grandson Ling, not the surname-plus-name Sun Ling.
His ancestor Zhang Jiang had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhe; a great-grandson's state became governor of Yulin and moved to Guanghan, whereupon they took the clan name from the fief.
His ancestor Zhang Jiang had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhe; great-grandson Guo became governor of Yulin and moved to Guanghan, whereupon they took the clan name from the fief.
曾孫國 is the personal name Guo (great-grandson Guo), not “a great-grandson’s state.”
